novel_features.name: Cross-base SQL over local mirror
novel_features.description: Run arbitrary SQL over a local SQLite mirror of one or more Airtable bases. Tables surface as `<base_slug>__<table_slug>`; linked-record arrays are stored as JSON columns you can `json_each()` over.
novel_features.rationale: Requires the local SQLite mirror this CLI builds with `sync` plus cross-table joining by linked-record IDs. Airtable has no API or UI for cross-base joins; SDKs return one table at a time.
novel_features.example: airtable-pp-cli query "SELECT a.name, COUNT(p.id) FROM accounts__customers a JOIN pipeline__opps p ON p.account_id = a.id GROUP BY a.name" --db ./airtable.db --agent
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent needs an answer that joins records across two or more tables (or bases) and the user has already synced, this is one local SQL query instead of two paginated REST round-trips plus client-side stitching.

novel_features.name: What-changed analytics window
novel_features.description: Joins the synced webhook_payloads table with the current records snapshot to report what fields changed across a base in the last N hours/days, grouped by table, field, or actor.
novel_features.rationale: No single Airtable API call returns 'what changed in the last 7 days'. Webhook payloads carry the events; this command turns them into a queryable changelog.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Agents and digest-builders can answer 'what's new since Friday' without setting up a webhook receiver or scraping per-record revision history.

novel_features.name: Stale-record finder
novel_features.description: Find records older than a duration, optionally filtered by a singleSelect status field, joined against the local cache's last_modified_time.
novel_features.rationale: Airtable formula language cannot cleanly express 'older than 30 days AND status=X' across views. Local SQL trivially can.
novel_features.example: airtable-pp-cli stale appXXX tblYYY --field Status --equals Draft --older-than 30d --db ./airtable.db --json
novel_features.why_it_matters: Drives content-calendar audits, follow-up reminders, and stale-deal sweeps without burning rate-limit budget on a full table scan every time.

novel_features.name: Schema-drift watcher (multi-base)
novel_features.description: Compare cached schemas of every base under the active profile against a fresh fan-out of `bases get_schema`; report added, removed, and renamed tables and fields. Exit 1 on drift for CI.
novel_features.rationale: airtable-mcp-server has no drift watcher. `schema diff` (absorbed) covers one base; `schema drift` fans across all bases under a profile.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Catches the 'someone added a singleSelect choice and broke our ETL' failure mode that hits multi-base setups every week.

novel_features.name: Webhook fleet manager
novel_features.description: List every webhook on every base under the active profile (or across `--all-profiles`), sorted by time-until-expiration, with last-payload age.
novel_features.rationale: No existing CLI or MCP exposes any webhook surface; fleet-level visibility is required to operate webhooks reliably across tenants.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Integration engineers managing webhooks across many bases see expirations and silent failures in one report instead of N lookups.

novel_features.name: Linked-record graph traversal
novel_features.description: Walk linked-record relationships from a starting record up to a depth limit; render as a tree (`--pretty`) or as ndjson edges (`--json`).
novel_features.rationale: Recursive linked-record walks require many sequential API calls to do live; doing them over the local mirror is instant and offline.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Lets agents resolve 'what's connected to this record' in one offline call, instead of pagination loops that trip the 5 req/sec rate limit.

novel_features.name: Record revision history from webhook payloads
novel_features.description: Reconstruct a record's edit timeline (field-level diffs in cursor order) from the synced webhook_payloads table.
novel_features.rationale: Revision history is UI-only in Airtable. Webhook payloads carry per-field change events; this command stitches them into a timeline.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Auditing 'who changed Status from Open to Won, when' becomes a single command instead of a clickthrough in the web UI.

narrative.headline: Every Airtable surface a CLI should have — plus a local SQLite mirror, cross-base SQL, and webhook tooling no SDK ships.
narrative.value_prop: Airtable's official SDKs stop at REST pass-through; the community CLIs and MCP servers do the same. airtable-pp-cli absorbs every endpoint (records, schema, webhooks, comments, workspaces) with proactive 5-req/sec rate-budget tracking, then adds a local SQLite mirror you can `query` with raw SQL, a `webhooks fleet` view that no existing tool offers, and a `history record` reconstructor that turns webhook payloads into a real audit log.
narrative.auth_narrative: Set `AIRTABLE_PAT` to a personal access token from airtable.com/create/tokens. Recommended scopes: `data.records:read`, `data.records:write`, `schema.bases:read`, `webhook:manage` for full functionality; `user.email:read` for the `whoami` health check. The CLI uses Bearer-token auth on every call and never persists the token to disk — set it in the env or per-profile config.

quickstart.comment: Health check: confirms AIRTABLE_PAT is set and the CLI builds outgoing requests correctly. Safe to run without network.
First real call — lists every base your PAT can see. Pages auto-followed.
Dump a base's full table+field+view schema as JSON for your README or LLM prompt.
Pull records modified in the last week into a local SQLite mirror so `query`, `analytics`, `stale`, and `traverse` work offline.
Cross-table SQL against the mirror — the headline differentiator.

troubleshoots.fix: Token is expired or revoked. Regenerate at airtable.com/create/tokens, then re-export `AIRTABLE_PAT` and re-run `airtable-pp-cli whoami get`.
Airtable enforces 5 req/sec/base. The CLI auto-backs-off 30s on 429 by default; lower concurrency further with `--retry-base-ms 1000` or split the sync by resource with `sync --resources records`.

troubleshoots.symptom: records create returns INVALID_VALUE_FOR_COLUMN on a singleSelect
troubleshoots.fix: Use `airtable-pp-cli records create appXXX tblYYY --fields '{...}' --dry-run` first — it validates against the cached schema and reports the exact field error.
Webhook may have expired (7-day TTL by default). Run `airtable-pp-cli webhooks fleet` to see expirations across all bases; refresh with `airtable-pp-cli webhooks refresh appXXX achXXX`.

narrative.when_to_use: Use airtable-pp-cli when an agent or script needs to read or write Airtable records reliably under the 5-req/sec-per-base rate limit, when you need cross-table or cross-base SQL over your data, when you need to operate webhooks across multiple bases or tenants, or when you need an audit trail of record changes that the Airtable UI hides behind clickthroughs. The local SQLite mirror is especially valuable for agents that re-query the same records repeatedly — sync once, query forever.

recipes.title: Sync a base and query it with SQL
recipes.command: airtable-pp-cli sync --resources records --since 7d --db ./airtable.db && airtable-pp-cli query "SELECT name, status FROM appXXX__customers WHERE last_modified_time > datetime('now','-1 day')" --db ./airtable.db --json
recipes.explanation: Pulls the last week of record changes into SQLite, then runs raw SQL against the mirror — no API round-trip for the query.

recipes.title: Audit what changed across a base since Friday
recipes.explanation: Joins webhook_payloads with current records to report grouped change counts; perfect for Monday-morning digest scripts.

recipes.title: Bulk upsert from a JSON file with progress
recipes.command: airtable-pp-cli records bulk-upsert appXXX tblYYY --records-file ./customers.json --merge-on Email --batch-progress
recipes.explanation: Auto-batches the input into 10-record chunks (Airtable per-request cap) and emits JSON progress lines on stderr per batch.

recipes.title: Surface deeply nested webhook payload data for an agent
recipes.explanation: Webhook payloads are deeply nested; `--select` with dotted paths narrows the response so an agent doesn't burn context parsing irrelevant fields. Pair `--agent` with `--select` on any nested response.

recipes.title: Find stale Draft articles older than 30 days
recipes.command: airtable-pp-cli stale appXXX tblYYY --field Status --equals Draft --older-than 30d --db ./airtable.db --pretty
recipes.explanation: Local query against the synced records cache — no API call, no rate-limit consumption, suitable to run on a cron.
